propositions: A new plan-review criterion T15 (overlay-derisk) must be added to reward proving risky runtime mechanisms via fast out-of-loop experiments before committing them into slow automated delivery loops.

T15 applies when a mechanism is delivered through an automated pipeline, one pass is slow or costly, and correctness depends on actual runtime behavior (boot, auth, connectivity, readiness) that static checks cannot validate.

T15 requires findings when applicable: naming the specific risk, committing to a fast proof path (local/emulated or manual probe against the real target), proving before codifying into the slow loop, and scoped cleanup of transient artifacts.

T10's rubric must be partitioned to explicitly exclude transient de-risk experiments from its durable-infrastructure scope, preventing overlap between the transient experiment phase and production-hardening evaluation.
The criterion must be rendered by `rebar explain T15`, included in regenerated plan-review-criteria-guide documentation, and guidance must appear in the writing-a-passing-plan author guide.
